Hit = E' > 0.001 (the kernel's timing threshold): ~13 of 99 detectors read out per shower (4–5 triangles)
ghosts cut ~10×: N = 99 at 10 µs, 3.2 → 0.3 per shower (two background muons can still open a triangle)
No noise / 128 ns: costs some pointing (N = 99, r = 25 m: 5.2 → 3.8% within 1°): lone weak hits are thrown away
1 µs: about even with reading everything (3.7 vs 3.6% at r = 25 m; 4.8 vs 4.8% at r = 100 m)
10 µs: the local trigger wins clearly: r = 25 m 0.4 → 2.2%, r = 500 m 0.5 → 4.0% (grid of 99, no local trigger: 0.6%)
So a 2-of-3 coincidence at a low threshold is the right tool for long windows; at ≤ 1 µs it costs little or nothing
Caveat: the clean recon was never trained on zeroed triangles; fine-tuning on this readout could recover more
